chunks: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: A blind man and a weak woman are with a Bedouin camel-driver, and when he departs with them from ʿArafāt, he passes on with them as they are to Minā and does not stop with them at Jamʿ.
So he said: “Have they not prayed there? Then that has sufficed them.”
I said: What if they did not pray there?
He said: “They remembered Allah, Mighty and Majestic, there; so if they had remembered Allah, Mighty and Majestic, there, then that has sufficed them.”

key_terms.عَرَفَاتٍ: ʿArafāt, the hajj station from which pilgrims depart
key_terms.مِنًى: Minā, the destination reached after departing

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for weak or disabled pilgrims who do not properly stop at Jamʿ (Muzdalifah) during hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning vulnerable pilgrims who are taken from ʿArafāt to Minā without stopping properly at Jamʿ (Muzdalifah). It indicates that if they performed salat there, or at least engaged in dhikr of Allah there, that was sufficient for them in fulfilling the required observance.
